title: Unpack a snap-shut egg carton into a basket without breaking an egg
instruction: Open the egg carton and put all six eggs in the basket, setting each one down gently on the cloth. A dropped egg is a broken egg.
context: Emptying a carton of eggs into a bowl or basket is an everyday kitchen job. Three things make it hard for a robot. The lid is snapped shut and the loaded carton weighs 380 g: the snap needs a 3 N pull at the lid's tab, but 1.5 N there already lifts the carton, so the other hand has to hold the base down. The eggs stand in cups with 1 mm of clearance and 18 mm between the two rows at cap height, against fingers 10 mm thick, so an egg can only be taken by its cap. And an egg rolls and breaks: one that falls more than 3 cm scores nothing, so the carton cannot be tipped out. Unlike egg-packing and egg-holder tasks, which place loose eggs into cups, here the eggs start inside a closed, latched package and have to come out of it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A is given first, layout B in brackets. Carton: a half-dozen (2 x 3) moulded-pulp egg carton, grey, 14.6 cm long, 11.0 cm deep and 6.9 cm tall closed, 32 g empty (base 20 g, lid 12 g). Centre at x 28.0, y -4.0 [B: x 26.5, y -2.5], long side across the table, hinge on the side toward the arms, so the lid opens toward them and comes to rest lying open at 180 degrees. The base is 4.2 cm tall with six cups, each 4.5 cm square inside and 3.9 cm deep, 4.8 cm apart along the carton and 6.0 cm apart across it; each cup narrows to a 4.0 cm square seat in its lower 1.75 cm. The lid is 2.7 cm tall. A two-button snap holds the lid shut and opens at a 3 N pull on the lid's tab. Lid pull tab: 3.0 cm wide, 3.5 cm long, 3 mm thick, sticking out level from the lid's far edge, 2.5 cm right of the carton's middle. Base thumb tab: 3.0 cm wide, 2.5 cm long, 3 mm thick, sticking out from the base's far edge level with the top of the base, 5.5 cm left of the carton's middle, propped on the table by a rib beneath it. Eggs: six white large hen's eggs, 43 mm across, 57 mm long, 58 g each, one standing in each cup with its top 2.2 cm above the cup walls. The loaded carton weighs 380 g. Basket: wicker, fixed to the table, 20 x 25 cm inside (25 cm across the table), walls 6 mm thick, rim 4.5 cm above the table, lined with a blue cloth whose top is 1.0 cm above the table. Centre at x 30.0, y -26.2 [B: x 28.5, y -25.2]. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: a photo of the end state, a look at each egg before and after the trial, and the trial video. Score = (number of eggs that count) / 6, read at the end of the run. An egg counts when all four hold. (1) It is unbroken: no crack or leak on inspection. In simulation, where the eggs are rigid, an egg is broken for the rest of the trial once it hits anything at more than 0.77 m/s, the speed a 3 cm free fall ends at. (2) It rests on the basket's cloth lining: its centre is inside the basket's walls and its lowest point is within 4 mm of the lining. An egg lying on other eggs or on the rim does not count, and an egg still in a cup of the carton does not count wherever the carton is. (3) It is still: moving slower than 5 cm/s. (4) It has been let go: no gripper's grasp point is within 4 cm of the egg's centre. So 1.0 for six eggs, 0.83 for five, 0.67 for four, 0.5 for three, 0.33 for two, 0.17 for one, else 0. Opening the lid alone earns nothing.
reset_notes: Replace any cracked egg. Stand the six eggs in the cups, close the lid until both buttons snap, and put the carton back on its marks with the hinge toward the arms. Empty the basket and smooth its cloth.
fidelity: Eggs are rigid 43 x 57 mm capsules of 58 g and cannot crack: one is marked broken if it hits anything at over 0.77 m/s (a 3 cm fall). Grip force is not judged. The carton is rigid, with square cups. Its two-button snap is a spring at the hinge that lets go for good once the lid has turned 4 degrees (3 N at the tab). The basket's cloth is a rigid plate; damping on the eggs stands in for the cloth's resistance to rolling.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the carton was never opened; the right gripper went into the empty basket and stayed there); demo: 1.0 (all six eggs lying on the cloth, unbroken, at step 1,865)
